import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 507

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/507](https://www.erdosproblems.com/507)
- [CPZ23] Cohen, Alex, Cosmin Pohoata, and Dmitrii Zakharov. "A new upper bound for the Heilbronn
  triangle problem." arXiv preprint arXiv:2305.18253 (2023).
- [CPZ24] Cohen, Alex, Cosmin Pohoata, and Dmitrii Zakharov. "Lower bounds for incidences."
  Inventiones mathematicae (2025): 1-74.
- [KPS82] Komlós, János, János Pintz, and Endre Szemerédi. "A lower bound for Heilbronn's problem."
  Journal of the London Mathematical Society 2.1 (1982): 13-24.
- [KPS81] Komlós, János, János Pintz, and Endre Szemerédi. "On Heilbronn's triangle problem."
  Journal of the London Mathematical Society 2.3 (1981): 385-396.
-/

open Asymptotics Filter Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos507

/--
The minimum area of a triangle determined by three distinct points in a set `S`.
-/
noncomputable def minTriangleArea (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℝ :=
  sInf {EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area (t.points 0) (t.points 1) (t.points 2) |
    (t : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ²) (_ : ∀ i, t.points i ∈ S)}

/--
$\alpha(n)$ is the supremum of `minTriangleArea S` over all sets `S` of $n$ points in the unit disk.
-/
noncomputable def α (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (minTriangleArea '' { S : Finset ℝ² |
    S.card = n ∧ ↑S ⊆ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1 ∧ ¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²) })

/--
Current best lower bound [KPS82].
-/
noncomputable def lowerBest (n : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.log n / (n : ℝ) ^ 2

/--
The "Barrier" function: n^(-7/6) used for the best upper bound [CPZ24].
-/
noncomputable def upperBarrier (n : ℕ) : ℝ := 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ ((7 : ℝ) / 6)

/--
Let $\alpha(n)$ be such that every set of $n$ points in the unit disk contains three points which
determine a triangle of area at most $\alpha(n)$. Estimate $\alpha(n)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.equivalent:
    α ~[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Estimate a lower bound for$\alpha(n)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.lower:
    let ans := (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
    (lowerBest =o[atTop] ans) ∧ (ans ≪ α) := by
  sorry

/--
Estimate an upper bound for$\alpha(n)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.upper:
    let ans := (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
    (α ≪ ans) ∧ (ans =o[atTop] upperBarrier) := by
  sorry

/--
It is trivial that $\alpha(n) \ll 1/n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.variants.upper_trivial : α ≪ (fun n ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős observed that $\alpha(n) \gg 1/n^2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.variants.lower_erdos : α ≫ (fun n ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
  sorry

/--
Current best lower bound [KPS82].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.variants.lower_kps82 : lowerBest ≪ α := by
  sorry

/--
Current best upper bound [CPZ24]: $\alpha(n) \ll n^{-7/6 + o(1)}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51]
theorem erdos_507.variants.upper_cpz24 :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
    α ≪ (fun n ↦ upperBarrier n * (n : ℝ) ^ o n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos507

findings.description: The infimum uses signed area instead of ordinary nonnegative area. `EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area` is an oriented determinant divided by 2 (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean:192–199), and `Affine.Triangle` allows both orientations. Thus, for a noncollinear finite set, this infimum is the negative of its largest triangle area, not its smallest triangle area. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved that the set {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)} has `minTriangleArea = -1/2`, and, by shrinking admissible configurations, that `Erdos507.α n = 0` for every n. These proofs use no sorry axioms. Consequently the main estimation and improved-upper-bound statements admit the explicit answer zero, while the stated Erdős lower bound is false (also refuted in Lean).
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/507 asks for the triangle-area threshold guaranteed in every n-point set in the unit disk and records α(n) ≫ 1/n² and (log n)/n² ≪ α(n). CPZ23, arXiv:2305.18253, Introduction, defines the corresponding extremal quantity using ordinary triangle areas and explains the positive lower bound using lattice triangles of area at least 1/(2p²).
findings.suggested_fix: Apply absolute value to each individual `EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area` before taking the infimum. Do not take the absolute value of the final infimum: that would produce a maximum area. Also address the independent collinear-triple exclusion described in the other finding.

findings.description: `Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ²` requires three affinely independent points, not merely three distinct points. It therefore excludes collinear triples, whose area must count as zero. The condition `¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)` in `α` does not repair this: it only says the entire set is not on one line. For S = {(0,0),(1/2,0),(1,0),(0,1)}, I verified in Lean that S is an admissible four-point configuration. Its correct minimum area is 0, whereas taking absolute values but retaining the `Affine.Triangle` indexing gives 1/4; both values were proved in the scratch file. This is not just a finite-input discrepancy: n−1 equally spaced points on [0,1]×{0}, together with (0,1), have minimum nondegenerate area 1/(2(n−2)). Such configurations would invalidate the cited asymptotic upper bound even after the sign issue is fixed.
findings.source_evidence: The Definition section of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heilbronn_triangle_problem, linked by the cited Erdős page, explicitly says: “When three of the placed points lie on a line, they are considered as forming a degenerate triangle whose area is defined to be zero.” CPZ24, arXiv:2409.07658v2, §1.3, states its upper bound for every n-point set, with no general-position assumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Range over injective point functions rather than affine simplices, including collinear triples: `sInf {|EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area (p 0) (p 1) (p 2)| | (p : Fin 3 → ℝ²) (_ : Function.Injective p) (_ : ∀ i, p i ∈ S)}`. The whole-set noncollinearity restriction in `α` can then be removed; for n ≥ 3, removing it merely restores configurations whose correct minimum is zero.

reformulations.difference: The Erdős page writes the upper bound as α(n) ≪ 1/n^(7/6+o(1)); Lean uses an existential sequence o tending to zero and the expression `upperBarrier n * (n : ℝ) ^ o n`. This entry concerns only the exponent encoding, not the defective definition of α.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 0, `upperBarrier n * n^(o n) = 1/n^(7/6-o n)`. Negating the sequence o preserves convergence to zero and gives a bijection between witnesses for the two formulations. The exceptional input n = 0 is irrelevant at `atTop`. The generic equivalence for an arbitrary function f was proved without sorry axioms as `Review507.upper_o_reformulation` in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18253; https://arxiv.org/e-print/2305.18253 — CPZ23, LaTeX Introduction and relevant concluding remarks
https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07658; https://arxiv.org/e-print/2409.07658 — CPZ24 v2, especially §§1.2–1.3 and the k-gon definition
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00222-025-01331-2 — published CPZ24 abstract and bibliographic information
https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~komlos/ — consulted while looking for accessible original papers
Local STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md; past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr01220.md, pr01903.md, pr04290.md, pr04057.md

Local FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean and Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean; Mathlib affine-simplex, collinearity, asymptotics, real supremum/infimum, Euclidean-space, and real-power definitions
review.notes: Reviewed all four definitions and seven theorem statements. The findings are reported at their shared root definition rather than duplicated for every dependent theorem. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles cleanly with the prescribed Lean command and proves the sign counterexample, α ≡ 0, the negation of the Erdős lower-bound statement, and the collinear-triple counterexample after an absolute-value-only repair. Boundary checks also confirmed minTriangleArea ∅ = 0, α(0)=α(1)=α(2)=0, lowerBest(0)=lowerBest(1)=0, and upperBarrier(0)=0, upperBarrier(1)=1; these finite initial cases cause no additional asymptotic defect. The source still marks the estimation problem open and records the same known bounds. The original KPS81/KPS82 publisher pages and PDFs were blocked by Cloudflare; their relevant bounds were checked against the Erdős page and CPZ23's Introduction.

submission.summary: Corrected both defects by taking absolute triangle areas over injective triples of points, so collinear triples are included with area zero. Updated the definition's docstring and left all other declarations unchanged. The required compilation succeeds with only existing `sorry` warnings; scratch regression proofs confirm nonnegativity and the expected minima of 1/2 and 0 for the two test configurations, without using sorry axioms.
